ARSCC.title: Character Creator
ARSCC.restartConfirm: Discard this draft and start over?
ARSCC.variantMismatch: This world uses the ARS variant "{world}". A character made with these rules expects "{chosen}": ability tables, attacks and initiative come from the world setting.
ARSCC.osricNote: Numbers follow the OSRIC 3.0 Player Guide. Ability and spell descriptions come from the OSRIC compendium, which still follows 2.2.
ARSCC.noContent: No Item compendium is visible. The wizard will use its built-in tables; enable the OSRIC Compendium module for full content.
ARSCC.name: Name
ARSCC.thiefNote: ARS adds Dexterity, race and armor adjustments when the skill is rolled. Totals are for no armor bonus.
ARSCC.noSpells: No arcane spell was found in the visible compendiums. Add spells on the character sheet later.
ARSCC.cartEmpty: Nothing bought yet. Choose items from the list.
ARSCC.viaGm: You cannot create actors, so the GM will be asked to confirm.
ARSCC.playersDisabled: The GM has not opened character creation to players.
ARSCC.noGm: No GM is connected to create the character.
ARSCC.waitingGm: Waiting for the GM to confirm the character.
ARSCC.gmDeclined: The GM did not confirm the character. Your draft is still saved.
ARSCC.missingItems: Some items could not be found and were left out: {list}
ARSCC.createFailed: The character could not be created: {error}

rulesetHints.add2e: Priests, specialists, bards and nonweapon proficiencies.

methods.3d6twice: 3d6 twice, keep the best, in order
methods.3d6x6each: 3d6 six times per ability, keep the best

methodHints.3d6order: Roll 3d6 for each ability in order.
methodHints.3d6twice: Roll 3d6 twice for each ability and keep the higher.
methodHints.3d6x6each: Roll 3d6 six times for each ability and keep the highest.
methodHints.3d6arrange: Roll 3d6 six times and assign the results.
methodHints.3d6twiceArrange: Roll 3d6 twice, six times over; keep the higher of each pair and assign.
methodHints.4d6drop: Roll 4d6 six times, drop the lowest die, and assign the results.
methodHints.3d6x12: Roll 3d6 twelve times, keep the six best and assign.
methodHints.3d6x12sets: Roll twelve complete characters and choose one.
methodHints.dicepool: Every ability starts at 8. Add whole dice to abilities; none may pass 18.
methodHints.manual: Type the scores before racial adjustment (3 to 18).
methodHints.4d6order: Roll 4d6 for each ability in order and drop the lowest die.

reasons.npcOnly: The tables list this pairing for NPCs only; ask your GM.

issues.abilitiesIncomplete: Roll or assign all six abilities.
issues.raceNotAllowed: The scores do not qualify for this race.
issues.classNotAllowed: {cls} is not available to this character.
issues.comboNotAllowed: This class combination is not allowed.
issues.npcOnly: The tables list this race and class for NPCs only.
issues.alignmentMissing: Choose an alignment the classes allow.
issues.thiefCap: No skill may receive more than {value} points.
issues.thief95: Points cannot raise a skill above 95%.
issues.spellsUnder: {value} more spell(s) suggested for the spellbook.
issues.spellsOver: More than the {value} spells usually granted.
issues.spellsMax: Intelligence allows at most {value} spells per level.
issues.goldOver: Purchases cost more than the gold available.
issues.ageMissing: Set the age: it adjusts ability scores.

allowPlayers.name: Players can use the creator
allowPlayers.hint: Show the button to players. Without permission to create actors, they ask the GM to confirm.

lockRuleset.name: Lock rules to the world variant
lockRuleset.hint: Only allow the rules that match the ARS system variant.

allowManual.name: Players can type values
allowManual.hint: Let players enter ability scores, exceptional strength and gold instead of rolling.

maxRerolls.name: Ability roll limit
maxRerolls.hint: How many times abilities can be rolled per character. 0 is unlimited; any other value also limits hit points, gold and exceptional strength to one roll for players.

sourcePacks.name: Compendiums to use
sourcePacks.hint: Comma-separated ids such as osric-compendium.items, in order of priority. Empty uses every visible Item compendium.
